title: Abba Moses and the Leaking Jug
text:
Abba Moses, called the Ethiopian or the Black, had been a slave and, by tradition, the leader of a band of robbers before he became a monk in the Egyptian desert of Scetis. In time he was one of its most respected elders.

Once a brother at Scetis committed a fault. The monks called a council to judge him and sent for Abba Moses, but he would not come. Then the priest sent someone to tell him, "Come, everyone is waiting for you."

So Moses got up and went. He took a jug that leaked, filled it with water and carried it with him. In later retellings it is a basket full of sand that ran out through the holes as he walked.

The brothers came out to meet him and asked, "What is this, Father?" The old man said, "My sins are running out behind me, and I do not see them. And today I am coming to judge the faults of someone else."

When they heard this, they said nothing more to the brother and forgave him.
lesson: When you feel ready to judge someone, remember the faults you no longer notice in yourself. Humility makes forgiveness easier.
people: Abba Moses the Ethiopian, the monks of Scetis
source: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Apophthegmata Patrum), alphabetical collection, Moses 2
